basics.name: Jordan Lee
basics.headline: Senior Product Manager, Digital Onboarding & Growth

resume.summary: Product manager with 8+ years in fintech and insurance, turning messy customer journeys into measurable digital products. I lead cross-functional squads from discovery to launch, write the business case, and own the adoption metrics after go-live.

bullets: Own the end-to-end account opening experience across web and mobile for 1.2M retail clients, leading two squads (11 engineers, 2 designers, 1 analyst).
Rebuilt identity verification and funding steps; onboarding completion rose from 54% to 71% in three quarters and drop-off support calls fell 38%.
Wrote the business case that secured $4.8M in multi-year funding for a reusable onboarding platform now used by three product lines.
Introduced an experimentation cadence (weekly A/B readouts, guardrail metrics) that shipped 23 tests in 2025 with a 35% win rate.
Partnered with Legal, Privacy and Risk to launch e-signature and digital ID in Quebec, including a Privacy Impact Assessment and French-language content review.
Launched digital first notice of loss for auto and home claims; 46% of claims filed digitally within 12 months, up from 9%.
Led a vendor selection and integration for claims status notifications, cutting "where is my claim" calls by 27%.
Defined the claims experience roadmap and quarterly OKRs with Operations, IT and the contact centre; ran monthly business reviews with the VP Claims.
Owned go-live and a 6-week hypercare period for the new claims portal, triaging 140+ issues with a zero-P1 launch.
Owned activation and trial-to-paid conversion for an SMB bookkeeping app; trial conversion improved from 11% to 17%.
Built the first product analytics stack (event taxonomy, funnels, cohort dashboards) with Amplitude and SQL.
Ran pricing and packaging tests with Marketing and Sales that lifted average revenue per account 14%.
Mapped customer and operations processes for bank and insurer clients; built business cases and current/future-state journeys for digital transformation programs.

projects.description: Personal project. Built a small web app with Claude and Supabase that helps Ontario renters compare leases and track maintenance requests; 600 monthly users.

brand.line: Product manager who turns messy customer journeys into measurable digital products, from business case to post-launch adoption.

pitch.s15: I'm a product manager who fixes the parts of a customer journey where people give up. At Maplewave I took digital onboarding completion from 54% to 71%.
pitch.s30: I'm a product manager with 8 years in fintech and insurance. I'm best at the messy middle: finding where customers drop off, building the business case, and leading squads through launch. At Maplewave Financial I rebuilt account opening and took completion from 54% to 71%, and before that I launched digital claims at Harbourline Insurance.
pitch.s60: I'm a product manager with 8 years in fintech and insurance, and I'm happiest in the messy middle of a customer journey. I started as a business analyst mapping processes for banks, moved into growth at a Series A startup where I learned to live in the data, then led claims experience at Harbourline Insurance, where digital claims went from 9% to 46% in a year. Today at Maplewave Financial I own digital onboarding for 1.2 million clients: I rebuilt identity verification and funding, took completion from 54% to 71%, and secured $4.8M to turn it into a platform. I'm looking for a senior product role where I own outcomes, not just a backlog.

stories.title: Rescuing a stalled onboarding redesign
stories.situation: Maplewave's account opening redesign had slipped two quarters and completion was stuck at 54%. Leadership was close to pausing it.
stories.task: Get the program back on track and show a measurable lift within two quarters.
stories.action: I paired funnel data with 14 customer interviews, found identity verification caused 60% of drop-off, cut the scope to the three worst steps, and shipped them behind experiments with weekly readouts to the VP.
stories.result: Completion rose to 71% in three quarters, support calls about onboarding fell 38%, and the program secured $4.8M of follow-on funding.

stories.title: Launching digital claims with zero P1s
stories.situation: Harbourline's new claims portal had to replace a paper-and-phone process before a fixed regulatory date.
stories.task: Own the launch and keep claims flowing through cut-over.
stories.action: I ran a phased rollout by province, set up a daily hypercare stand-up with IT, Operations and the vendor, and published a single issue tracker the contact centre could see.
stories.result: We went live on date with zero P1 incidents, resolved 140+ issues in a 6-week hypercare period, and reached 46% digital claims within a year.

stories.title: A pricing test that failed, and what it taught me
stories.situation: At Ledgerly I was confident a lower entry price would grow paid accounts.
stories.task: Prove it with a clean pricing experiment.
stories.action: We ran the test for four weeks. Signups rose but revenue per account dropped and churn rose in the cheaper tier. I shared the result openly and proposed a packaging test instead.
stories.result: The packaging change lifted revenue per account 14%. I now define guardrail metrics before every pricing test.

stories.title: Getting Legal and Risk to yes on e-signature
stories.situation: Digital ID and e-signature for Quebec clients had been blocked for a year by privacy and language concerns.
stories.task: Find a launch path Legal, Privacy and Risk could all support.
stories.action: I ran the Privacy Impact Assessment myself, brought Legal into design reviews early, and proposed a limited launch with extra monitoring.
stories.result: Approved in 8 weeks; Quebec clients can now open accounts fully online.
